intro: Barbados, the easternmost Caribbean island, was a key British sugar colony and became a republic in 2021.

chapters.title: English settlement
text: The island was largely uninhabited when English settlers arrived in 1627. It was the first English colony to build a sugar economy on the labour of enslaved Africans, a model copied across the Caribbean.

chapters.title: Rebellion and freedom
text: In 1816 an enslaved man named Bussa led a large rebellion. Slavery ended in the 1830s. Barbados became independent in 1966.

highlight.title: Bussa
highlight.text: Bussa is one of Barbados's national heroes.

chapters.title: A republic
text: On 30 November 2021 Barbados removed the British monarch as head of state and became a republic, with Sandra Mason as first president. Rihanna was named a national hero the same day.

keyTerms.meaning: A country with an elected head of state.
